answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players. 2. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next in B, and continue alternating A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player, so 7 Adults in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Board setup: ‘3 pods for 3–4 players’; lowest-numbered in A, next in B, alternate; all Locked. ‘3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.’

answers.answer: 1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objectives showing a player count above the actual player count. 2. Shuffle the decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective, kept hidden. 3. At the First Encounter, each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game, unseen. 4. Eggs do not trigger this choice; they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Crew setup steps 16 and First Encounter: filter higher-player-count cards, deal one of each; choose at first Intruder miniature appearance; ‘Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.’

answers.answer: 1. Discard the Action card being used and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2; the two other Action cards in hand cover that payment. 2. Contamination cards cannot be discarded to pay an Action cost. 3. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section.
answers.evidence: Actions: use the card and pay its cost with additional Action cards; Contamination cards can never pay. ‘If a card has two sections separated by “OR,” choose one.’

answers.answer: 1. Fire damage is taken after the Character finishes their own round, so they suffer 1 Light Wound then. 2. After passing, they cannot perform further Actions this Player Phase. 3. When passing, they may discard any number of cards from hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not cause this Character to take Fire damage again; it is assessed after their own round only.
answers.evidence: Player rounds: ‘A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound’; only after finishing their own round, and passing players take it once at end of their round. Passing bars further Actions and permits discarding any number of cards.

answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then remove that token to the box. Set the Room's Item count by rotating the tile so the token number faces the board's Item Counter; do not set a count for the Nest or Room Covered in Slime. 2. Resolve the token effect before the Noise roll: Silence suppresses the roll; Danger also suppresses it and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, puts Noise markers in every connected Corridor that lacks one. Other listed effects are Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or a Door in the entry Corridor. 3. If the destination is empty after entering and no effect suppressed the roll, roll for Noise. 4. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination Room, do not roll for Noise. 5. Silence does nothing unless the Character has Slime, in which case resolve Danger; Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders, and if there are none (or all are in Combat), places markers in all connected Corridors that lack one.
answers.evidence: Movement and Exploration tokens: flip/reveal/resolve and remove token; orient Item count; Silence and Danger suppress Noise; Noise roll only if no Character or Intruder is already there; Slime changes Silence to Danger.

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. 2. It cannot be used in Combat, and cannot be used if all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers. 3. Its normal Movement restrictions still apply, including that Closed Doors block passage. 4. A miniature cannot stop in a Corridor; characters and Intruders occupy Rooms only.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement cost 2, places Noise instead of rolling, unavailable in Combat/all destination Corridors marked; it follows normal restrictions including Closed Doors. Movement section: no one may stop in a Corridor.

answers.answer: 1. A Noise roll result that calls for a marker in a Corridor already holding one causes an Encounter instead. With a Technical Corridors Entrance, a number leading there places Noise on the shared Technical Corridors space, which counts for every Entrance; attempting to add a second marker there triggers the Encounter. 2. At an Encounter, discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including Technical Corridors if connected; draw a token from the bag and place the matching Intruder. 3. Compare its number with the triggering player's hand, counting both Action and Contamination cards: fewer cards than the number means a Surprise Attack against that Character. 4. Set a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag; a Blank instead restores Noise to each connected Corridor and is returned to the bag. 5. Yes, Contamination cards count in the hand comparison.
answers.evidence: Noise roll: placing where a marker already exists resolves an Encounter. Technical Corridors: shared marker and second-marker limit. Encounters: clear connected Noise, draw/place, compare against hand including Contamination; non-Blank token set aside; Blank restores Noise and returns.

answers.answer: 1. Danger moves all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with a Character into the destination Room. 2. If there are no eligible Intruders, or all are in Combat, place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one. 3. An Intruder moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it simply creates Combat. 4. With Slime, a Silence result becomes Danger.
answers.evidence: Danger: ‘move ALL eligible Intruders’; otherwise mark every connected Corridor lacking Noise. Encounter section says an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter. Slime converts Silence to Danger.

answers.answer: 1. For a Blank drawn during an Encounter, put a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without placing a miniature. 2. If it was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token if available. 3. In bag development, a Blank adds 1 Adult token if available, then the Blank is returned to the bag; this does not require the Blank to be the last token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: Blank restores connected Noise; if it was the last token add Adult if available; return Blank. Bag development: Blank adds an Adult if available and returns to bag.

answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders stay in their original Room and destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. 2. A destroyed Door lies flat and allows movement, and it cannot be Closed again except with the Plasma Torch Item. 3. An Intruder appearing because of a Noise roll is placed regardless of a Closed Door in that Corridor.
answers.evidence: Door rules: several Intruders moving from the same Room through a Closed Door destroy it simultaneously and all stay put; destroyed Doors permit movement and cannot be Closed except by Plasma Torch; Noise-triggered appearance ignores Closed Doors.

answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature and all Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. 2. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. 3. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors; the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item are stated exceptions. 4. Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: an Intruder entering disappears, loses Injury markers, and returns to bag; Noise is not removed; characters have two listed exceptions; Doors cannot be placed there.

answers.answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card, requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo, targets one Intruder in your Room, and discards 1 Ammo before rolling. A blank die result misses without penalty. 2. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto the top of your Action discard pile, and targets one Intruder in your Room. 3. A Melee miss gives the Character 1 Serious Wound. 4. In Melee, a two-hit die result counts as one Injury; in Shooting, the double-hit result deals two Injuries before weapon modifications.
answers.evidence: Combat quick reference and Combat section: Shoot cost/ammo/target and blank miss; Melee cost, Contamination placement, miss wound; two hits count as one in melee, two Injuries when shooting.

answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies from 1 Injury. 2. For an Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card: it dies if the blood value is equal to or below its current Injury markers. 3. For a Queen, draw two cards, add their blood values, and compare the total the same way. 4. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass token in the Room; Larvae are the exception and leave no Carcass. 5. If a Retreat arrow appears during an Injury Effect check, resolve retreat instead of the numeric death check; for a Queen, either of its two cards showing Retreat causes the retreat.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death: Larva 1 Injury; Adult one blood check; Queen two summed checks; Carcass for every dead Intruder except Larvae. Retreat replaces numerical result; Queen/Breeder retreat if either card shows it.

answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room; the escaper is the target. 2. Each attack draws an Attack card and hits only if its symbol matches the attacking Intruder type; otherwise it misses. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4. If they survive, they complete the move to the neighboring Room, explore it if unexplored, and make a Noise roll if it is empty (unless an Exploration effect suppresses it).
answers.evidence: Character Escape: one separate attack per Intruder before movement; survive then move and resolve exploration/Noise; if die, Corpse stays in original Room. Intruder Attack: matching symbol hits, otherwise misses.

answers.answer: 1. With several Characters in the Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder or the next player in turn order. 2. Draw one Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder symbol means a hit and its effect resolves; otherwise it misses. 3. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target 1 Contamination card. 4. That Contamination card goes on top of the target's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack targeting and resolution; Infest (Larva attack); Contamination section specifies placement on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: 1. Dressing a Serious Wound does not prevent death from a further Wound when the Character already has 3 Serious Wounds; any additional Light or Serious Wound kills them. 2. Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death: third Light converts to Serious; three Serious plus any further Wound means death; dressing does not prevent it; Heal removes as specified; Corpse and Heavy Objects remain in Room.

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan Contamination cards in the Character's HAND and remove all non-Infected ones; an Infected result places a Larva on the board, and if one is already there the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes Slime. 2. Surgery scans cards in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva if present. 3. Surgery is a Room Action costing 2 Action cards; after it, suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all cards (including the whole hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck. The hand remains empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen/Shower scan all Contamination in HAND and remove non-Infected; Surgery scans deck/hand/discard and removes infected plus Larva, then Light Wound, auto-pass, shuffle all cards; Room Actions cost 2.

answers.answer: 1. In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee against them; each Injury destroys one Egg. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. 2. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. Whether a successful Egg Melee causes Contamination is unsupported by the summary, which says the manual does not uniquely settle it. 3. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg in that Room during each Fire Damage step. 4. Roll Noise after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. 5. When no Eggs remain in the Nest, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: attack/injury, Grenade and Molotov amounts, missed Egg Melee exception, per-attempt Noise, Fire effect, and Nest destruction are specified; successful Egg Melee Contamination is explicitly unresolved.

answers.answer: 1. To enter, use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); the Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that Section. First make a Noise roll; you cannot enter if an Intruder appears or is present in the Room, or if there is a Malfunction token there. 2. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not use a Character space. 3. After boarding, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase, or exit voluntarily for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. 4. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Section Room while you wait, all Characters in its Pods return to that Room. A second Character boarding a waiting Pod may launch it immediately with both aboard.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods: entry conditions and preceding Noise roll; capacity, Heavy Objects; launch/wait/pass/exit choices; Intruder return; second occupant may launch.

answers.answer: 1. The endgame Victory Check order is Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. 2. If two Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pods are already away. 3. If the destination is not Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. 4. Each surviving Character, including evacuated Pod passengers, checks Contamination: scan all cards in deck, discard, and hand; if any is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four, and any Contamination among those four kills. A Character carrying a Larva skips the initial Scan and directly does the shuffle-and-draw-four test. 5. Then surviving Characters reveal Objectives and win if requirements are met.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: ordered Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives; two Damaged Engines explode; non-Earth/Mars Quarantine exception; Contamination check applies to hibernating or evacuated Characters and Larva; launched Pods are away.
